pull_quotes.after_paragraph: The alternative is a fixed-price issue, where the company names a single price upfront and investors either take it or leave it.
pull_quotes.quote: Book-building is the opposite: the price is discovered from demand over a few days of bidding.
pull_quotes.rationale: Captures the core concept of price discovery in one sentence.

sidebars.body_markdown: In IPO bidding, you cannot apply for an arbitrary number of shares. Instead, you apply in 'lots' — a fixed number of shares determined by the company and its bankers. The lot size is set so that the minimum application value (the smallest amount you must commit) falls between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000. For example, if the price band is ₹200–₹240, the lot might be 60 shares, giving a minimum application of ₹12,000 (60 × ₹200). You can apply for one lot, two lots, three lots, and so on. The exact lot size is disclosed in the offer document and the price band advertisement.
sidebars.rationale: Explains the practical concept of lot size, which is not covered in the main text.
sidebars.title: What is a lot size?
